title: Debt Fund Taxation: Understanding Changes Before & After April 2023

faq.q: What exactly changed for debt funds on April 1, 2023?
faq.a: From April 1, 2023, all gains from debt mutual funds (and other non-equity oriented funds) purchased on or after this date are now treated as short-term capital gains, irrespective of the holding period, and taxed at your individual income tax slab rate.

faq.q: Does this change apply to all mutual funds?
faq.a: No, this change primarily impacts mutual funds that invest less than 35% of their corpus in equity shares of domestic companies. Equity-oriented mutual funds (investing 65% or more in Indian equities) continue with their existing tax treatment.

faq.q: What is indexation benefit, and why was it important?
faq.a: Indexation benefit adjusts the original cost of your investment for inflation over the holding period, reducing your taxable capital gain. It was crucial for long-term debt fund investments as it significantly lowered the effective tax paid on gains.

faq.q: If I already own debt funds bought before April 1, 2023, do the old rules still apply?
faq.a: Yes, for debt fund units purchased on or before March 31, 2023, the old tax rules continue to apply. This means you can still avail of the indexation benefit for long-term capital gains (held over 36 months).

faq.q: Are NRIs also affected by this change?
faq.a: Yes, the change in tax treatment applies universally to all investors, including Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), for debt fund investments made on or after April 1, 2023. Their gains will also be taxed at their applicable slab rates in India.

faq.q: Are there any debt-like instruments still offering indexation?
faq.a: As of now, the indexation benefit for long-term capital gains is largely restricted to equity-oriented funds (if held for over 12 months for 10% tax over ₹1 lakh) and certain other assets like real estate. For debt-like instruments, the direct indexation benefit on capital gains has been removed for most mutual fund categories.
